name: Daylio
summary: Mood tracker and micro-diary with 4.7★ rating for tracking emotional patterns
description: Daylio is a simple, ad-free mood tracker and micro-diary app. Track your mood, activities, and habits without typing. Identify patterns, triggers, and trends in your mental health with beautiful charts and statistics.
patient_summary: Daylio is a mood tracking app that helps you log how you're feeling each day using icons (no writing required). You tap your mood (rad, good, meh, bad, awful) and activities (work, exercise, socializing, etc.), and it creates charts showing patterns over time. Best for people with depression or bipolar disorder who want to track mood cycles, identify triggers, and share data with therapists. Not a treatment—it's a tracking tool.

sections.heading: What Daylio Does
sections.text: Daylio is a micro-diary and mood tracker. Every day, you log your mood (rad, good, meh, bad, awful—fully customizable) and activities (work, exercise, friends, etc.). You don't have to write anything—just tap icons. Over time, Daylio builds charts showing your mood patterns, correlations between activities and mood, and streaks. You can export data as PDF or CSV to share with your therapist.

sections.heading: How Well Does It Work?
sections.text: Mood tracking apps like Daylio are validated tools for increasing self-awareness and identifying patterns. Systematic reviews show that mood tracking supports behavioral activation therapy for depression and helps people with bipolar disorder detect episode changes early. Most effective when combined with professional treatment.
sections.patient_text: People who use Daylio consistently (daily for 2+ weeks) report noticing patterns they didn't see before—like 'I feel worse on days I don't exercise' or 'my mood drops after stressful work meetings.' This awareness helps guide lifestyle changes and therapy.

sections.heading: Who Should Use Daylio?
sections.text: Daylio is best for people who:
items: Have depression or bipolar disorder and want to track mood cycles
Are in therapy (especially CBT or behavioral activation) and need data to share
Want to identify triggers and patterns in their mood
Prefer quick, icon-based logging over writing long journal entries
Want to track multiple things (mood, activities, habits, symptoms)
Like seeing visual charts and statistics
not_recommended: People who want therapeutic guidance (this is just a tracker, not therapy)
Those who prefer writing long journal entries (use Day One or Journey instead)
People prone to rumination (may obsess over checking mood too often)
Those in acute crisis (need immediate professional help, not an app)

items.description: Tap your mood (5 levels by default: rad, good, meh, bad, awful) and add activities. Takes 10 seconds. No writing required. Fully customizable—change mood names, colors, and number of levels.
items.evidence: Low-friction logging = higher compliance. Quick check-ins are validated for mood tracking.

items.description: Tag activities for each mood entry (exercise, work, friends, sleep, etc.). Daylio correlates activities with mood to show patterns. Example: 'You feel better on days you exercise.'
items.evidence: Behavioral activation therapy relies on activity-mood correlations. Daylio automates this.

items.description: View mood trends over time (line charts, calendar heat maps, bar charts). See average mood per month, mood distribution, and activity correlations. Year-in-review feature.
items.evidence: Visualizations increase insight and pattern recognition.

items.description: Gamified tracking with streak counters. Motivates daily check-ins. See longest streak, current streak, etc.
items.evidence: Gamification increases app engagement and habit formation.

items.description: Export mood data to share with therapist or psychiatrist. PDF has charts and graphs. CSV is raw data for analysis.
items.evidence: Therapists often request mood logs. Export feature makes this seamless.

items.description: All data stored on your device by default. No account required. Optional cloud backup (encrypted). Maximum privacy.
items.evidence: Privacy-first design reduces data breach risk and increases trust.

items.description: Set reminders to log mood daily (morning, evening, or custom times). Notifications are gentle and customizable.
items.evidence: Reminders increase compliance with daily tracking.

sections.heading: Privacy & Data Security
sections.summary: Daylio is privacy-first. All data stored locally by default. No ads. No data selling. Grade: A-
items: All data stored on your device (not on external servers)
No account required for basic features
Secure PIN or biometric lock (fingerprint, Face ID)
data_collected: Email address (only if you enable cloud backup)
data_shared: Optional: Cloud backup (encrypted, stored on iCloud/Google Drive)
concerns: Cloud backup is optional—if you enable it, your mood data is on iCloud/Google Drive (encrypted but on their servers)
No HIPAA compliance (not a medical device)
If someone unlocks your phone, they can access your mood data (enable PIN lock)
sections.hipaa_note: Not HIPAA-compliant. Do not use for clinical records. If you export data to share with therapist, ensure secure transmission (encrypted email, patient portal).

sections.heading: How to Start Using Daylio
steps: Download from App Store (iOS) or Google Play (Android)
Open app—no account required to start
Customize your moods (keep default 5 levels or change names/colors)
Add your most common activities (work, exercise, friends, sleep, etc.)
Log your first mood entry—pick mood and tap activities
Set daily reminder notification (recommended for consistency)
After 7+ days, check Statistics tab to see patterns
tips: Log mood at the same time each day (e.g., before bed) for consistency
Don't overthink it—pick the mood that feels most accurate and move on
Add notes for context (optional, but helpful for therapy)
After 2 weeks, look for patterns in Charts—do certain activities correlate with better mood?
Export data monthly to share with therapist or psychiatrist
common_mistakes: Logging mood too many times per day (can increase anxiety and rumination—once daily is ideal)
Expecting instant insight (need 2+ weeks of data to see patterns)
Not customizing activities—use activities relevant to YOUR life
Forgetting to enable reminders (easy to fall off without notifications)
Not sharing data with therapist (that's the whole point!)

items.name: eMoods
items.comparison: Specifically designed for bipolar disorder. More clinical features (mania/depression scales). Less polished UI. Free with optional premium. Choose eMoods if you have bipolar and want bipolar-specific tracking.

items.name: Bearable
items.comparison: More comprehensive—track symptoms, medications, sleep, diet, etc. Better for chronic illness tracking. More complex interface. Choose Bearable if you want to track multiple health factors beyond mood.

items.name: Moodpath
items.comparison: Includes daily psychological questions and generates reports for therapists. More therapeutic guidance. Choose Moodpath if you want guided assessments, Daylio if you want simple mood logging.

faqs.a: Yes, Daylio is useful for depression, especially alongside therapy. It helps you track mood patterns, identify low mood triggers, and monitor activity levels (important for behavioral activation therapy). However, it's NOT a treatment—just a tracking tool. If you have depression, you still need therapy and/or medication.

faqs.q: Can Daylio help with bipolar disorder?
faqs.a: Yes. Daylio is excellent for bipolar disorder. Daily mood tracking helps you (and your psychiatrist) detect manic/hypomanic episodes early, monitor mood cycling, and adjust medications. Many bipolar patients use Daylio to create mood charts to share with their doctor. Critical for bipolar management.

Yes. Daylio has a generous free version with unlimited mood tracking, activities, basic stats, and data export. No ads. Premium ($24.99/year) adds advanced features like goals, photo attachments, multiple entries per day, and more. Most people are fine with free.

faqs.q: Does Daylio store my data in the cloud?
faqs.a: No, by default. All data is stored locally on your device. You don't need an account. Optional: You can enable cloud backup (encrypted) to iCloud (iOS) or Google Drive (Android). If you enable backup, your data is encrypted but stored on Apple/Google servers.

faqs.q: Can I share my Daylio data with my therapist?
faqs.a: Yes. Daylio has an export feature. Go to More > Export Data > PDF or CSV. PDF gives you charts and graphs to print or email. CSV is raw data for analysis. Many therapists request mood logs—Daylio makes this easy.

faqs.q: How often should I log my mood in Daylio?
faqs.a: Once daily is ideal. Pick a consistent time (e.g., before bed). Logging too frequently (multiple times per day) can increase anxiety and rumination. Once daily gives you enough data to see patterns without overthinking.

No. Daylio is not HIPAA-compliant and is not a medical device. It's a personal wellness app. If you export data to share with a therapist, use secure transmission (encrypted email, patient portal, or print in-office).

Yes. Daylio is rated 12+ (safe for teens). It's simple and icon-based, so younger teens can use it. Useful for teens with depression, anxiety, or mood instability to share data with parents or therapists. Younger kids may find it too abstract.

faqs.q: What's the difference between Daylio free and premium?
faqs.a: Free: Unlimited mood tracking, activities, basic stats, export, no ads. Premium ($24.99/year): Goals, multiple entries per day, photo attachments, mood-activity correlations, advanced charts, themes, unlimited cloud backup. Most people don't need premium.

faqs.q: Will Daylio help me feel better?
faqs.a: Indirectly. Daylio increases self-awareness by showing mood patterns and triggers. This insight can guide lifestyle changes (e.g., 'I feel better when I exercise') or help your therapist tailor treatment. But Daylio itself doesn't treat depression or anxiety—it's just a tracking tool.
